CASE FACTS:
French Party A and Dutch Party B agreed in writing that the Amsterdam courts would have exclusive jurisdiction over their sale-of-goods contract. B first brings a negative declaratory action in France; A then sues for payment in the Netherlands.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24] Exclusive jurisdiction
Article 24 assigns exclusive jurisdiction, regardless of the parties' domicile, for the listed subject matters.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25] Choice-of-court agreements
Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(b)] Sale and service performance place
For a sale of goods, Article 7(1)(b) uses the place where the goods were or should have been delivered; for services, it uses the place where the services were or should have been provided.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(1)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is rights in rem in, or tenancies of, immovable property are generally within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State where the property is situated, subject to the stated short private-tenancy exception.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(3)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is the validity of entries in public registers are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the register is kept.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(2)] Choice-of-court agreements
Electronic communication that provides a durable record of a jurisdiction agreement is equivalent to writing.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(4)] Choice-of-court agreements
A jurisdiction agreement has no legal force if it conflicts with the specified protective-jurisdiction provisions or purports to exclude a court having exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.27] Own-motion review of exclusive jurisdiction
When the courts of another Member State have exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24, the court seised must declare of its own motion that it has no jurisdiction.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

repair.prompt:
The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
Proceedings are filed in France in the morning and in Germany later the same day. Determine which court is first seised.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

Article 6 addresses jurisdiction over defendants not domiciled in a Member State, principally by reference to Member State law subject to specified Regulation exceptions.

Against a defendant not domiciled in a Member State, a person domiciled in a Member State may invoke that State's jurisdiction rules on the same basis as its nationals.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.62] Domicile of natural persons
Article 62 determines which domestic law a court applies when deciding whether a natural person is domiciled in a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.4(1)] General jurisdiction by defendant domicile
A person domiciled in a Member State is generally sued in the courts of that Member State, irrespective of nationality.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.6(1)] Defendant outside all Member States
Where a defendant is not domiciled in a Member State, jurisdiction is generally determined by the law of the Member State court seised, subject to specified exceptions.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.62(1)] Domicile of natural persons
To determine whether a party is domiciled in the Member State whose courts are seised, the court applies its own internal law.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.62(2)] Domicile of natural persons
If a party is not domiciled in the seised court's Member State, the court applies the law of another Member State to determine whether the party is domiciled there.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.18(1)] Jurisdiction for consumer contracts
A consumer may sue the other contracting party either in the courts of that party's Member State of domicile or, regardless of that party's domicile, in the courts for the place where the consumer is domiciled.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.18(2)] Jurisdiction for consumer contracts
The other contracting party may sue a consumer only in the courts of the Member State in which the consumer is domiciled.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.17(1)(c)] Consumer contract scope
The protective consumer-contract rules apply where the trader pursues or directs commercial activities to the consumer's Member State in the circumstances specified by this provision.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.19] Choice-of-court limits in consumer contracts
A choice-of-court agreement in a consumer contract may depart from the protective jurisdiction rules only under the conditions stated in this provision.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(4)] Choice-of-court agreements
A jurisdiction agreement has no legal force if it conflicts with the specified protective-jurisdiction provisions or purports to exclude a court having exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.26(2)] Jurisdiction by appearance
For specified weaker parties, jurisdiction based on appearance requires the court to ensure that the defendant was informed of the right to contest jurisdiction and of the consequences of appearing or not appearing.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(2)] Place of harmful event
In matters relating to tort or delict, proceedings may be brought in the courts for the place where the harmful event occurred or may occur.

CASE FACTS:
French Party A and Dutch Party B agreed in writing that the Amsterdam courts would have exclusive jurisdiction over their sale-of-goods contract. B first brings a negative declaratory action in France; A then sues for payment in the Netherlands.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24] Exclusive jurisdiction
Article 24 assigns exclusive jurisdiction, regardless of the parties' domicile, for the listed subject matters.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25] Choice-of-court agreements
Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(b)] Sale and service performance place
For a sale of goods, Article 7(1)(b) uses the place where the goods were or should have been delivered; for services, it uses the place where the services were or should have been provided.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(1)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is rights in rem in, or tenancies of, immovable property are generally within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State where the property is situated, subject to the stated short private-tenancy exception.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(3)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is the validity of entries in public registers are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the register is kept.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(2)] Choice-of-court agreements
Electronic communication that provides a durable record of a jurisdiction agreement is equivalent to writing.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(4)] Choice-of-court agreements
A jurisdiction agreement has no legal force if it conflicts with the specified protective-jurisdiction provisions or purports to exclude a court having exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.27] Own-motion review of exclusive jurisdiction
When the courts of another Member State have exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24, the court seised must declare of its own motion that it has no jurisdiction.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

CASE FACTS:
Proceedings are filed in France in the morning and in Germany later the same day. Determine which court is first seised.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

CASE FACTS:
A German court is first seised of A's contractual damages action against B. A Spanish court is later seised of a negative declaratory action involving the same parties and the same contract.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(2)] Place of harmful event
In matters relating to tort or delict, proceedings may be brought in the courts for the place where the harmful event occurred or may occur.

For purposes of the Regulation, a company or other legal person is domiciled at its central administration.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.63(1)(c)] Domicile of companies and legal persons
For purposes of the Regulation, a company or other legal person is domiciled at its principal place of business.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24] Exclusive jurisdiction
Article 24 assigns exclusive jurisdiction, regardless of the parties' domicile, for the listed subject matters.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25] Choice-of-court agreements
Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(1)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is rights in rem in, or tenancies of, immovable property are generally within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State where the property is situated, subject to the stated short private-tenancy exception.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(3)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is the validity of entries in public registers are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the register is kept.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(4)] Choice-of-court agreements
A jurisdiction agreement has no legal force if it conflicts with the specified protective-jurisdiction provisions or purports to exclude a court having exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.27] Own-motion review of exclusive jurisdiction
When the courts of another Member State have exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24, the court seised must declare of its own motion that it has no jurisdiction.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.63(1)(a)] Domicile of companies and legal persons
For purposes of the Regulation, a company or other legal person is domiciled at its statutory seat.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.63(1)(b)] Domicile of companies and legal persons
For purposes of the Regulation, a company or other legal person is domiciled at its central administration.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.63(1)(c)] Domicile of companies and legal persons
For purposes of the Regulation, a company or other legal person is domiciled at its principal place of business.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(b)] Sale and service performance place
For a sale of goods, Article 7(1)(b) uses the place where the goods were or should have been delivered; for services, it uses the place where the services were or should have been provided.

CASE FACTS:
A French court is first seised of a claim for contractual damages. A German court is later seised of a negative declaratory action concerning the same contract.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(2)] Place of harmful event
In matters relating to tort or delict, proceedings may be brought in the courts for the place where the harmful event occurred or may occur.

Proceedings concerned with the registration or validity of patents, trade marks, designs, or other similar rights required to be deposited or registered fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the deposit or registration has been applied for, has taken place, or is deemed to have taken place, irrespective of whether the issue is raised by way of an action or as a defence.

A counterclaim for revocation or for a declaration of invalidity may rely only on grounds for revocation or invalidity stated in the Regulation.

The time when a court is deemed seised depends on lodging the initiating document with the court or the authority responsible for service, provided the claimant takes the required subsequent steps.

CASE FACTS:
A German court hears a consumer-contract dispute. Consumer B, a French national, appears without contesting jurisdiction.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.26(1)] Appearance without jurisdiction objection
Apart from jurisdiction derived from other provisions of the Regulation, a court of a Member State before which a defendant enters an appearance has jurisdiction, except where the appearance was entered to contest jurisdiction or another court has exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.17(1)(c)] Consumer contract scope
The protective consumer-contract rules apply where the trader pursues or directs commercial activities to the consumer's Member State in the circumstances specified by this provision.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.18(1)] Jurisdiction for consumer contracts
A consumer may sue the other contracting party either in the courts of that party's Member State of domicile or, regardless of that party's domicile, in the courts for the place where the consumer is domiciled.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.18(2)] Jurisdiction for consumer contracts
The other contracting party may sue a consumer only in the courts of the Member State in which the consumer is domiciled.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.19] Choice-of-court limits in consumer contracts
A choice-of-court agreement in a consumer contract may depart from the protective jurisdiction rules only under the conditions stated in this provision.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(4)] Choice-of-court agreements
A jurisdiction agreement has no legal force if it conflicts with the specified protective-jurisdiction provisions or purports to exclude a court having exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.26(2)] Jurisdiction by appearance
For specified weaker parties, jurisdiction based on appearance requires the court to ensure that the defendant was informed of the right to contest jurisdiction and of the consequences of appearing or not appearing.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

A Polish court was first seised but later found that it lacked jurisdiction and dismissed the action. Proceedings concerning the same dispute had also been filed in the Netherlands shortly before that dismissal.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

Where a defendant is not domiciled in a Member State, jurisdiction is generally determined by the law of the Member State court seised, subject to specified exceptions.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(2)] Validity of companies and corporate decisions
Proceedings principally concerned with the validity, nullity, or dissolution of a company or the validity of decisions of its organs are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the company has its seat.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.4(1)] General jurisdiction by defendant domicile
A person domiciled in a Member State is generally sued in the courts of that Member State, irrespective of nationality.

repair.prompt:
The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
An Austrian court is first seised of A's contractual action against B but later finds that it lacks jurisdiction and dismisses the action. Proceedings concerning the same contract had been filed in Belgium shortly before the dismissal.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

repair.prompt:
The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
Party B was resident in Spain but recently moved away without a clearly established new long-term place of residence. Party A wishes to sue B in Spain to recover a loan.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.4(1)] General jurisdiction by defendant domicile
A person domiciled in a Member State is generally sued in the courts of that Member State, irrespective of nationality.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.62] Domicile of natural persons
Article 62 determines which domestic law a court applies when deciding whether a natural person is domiciled in a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.62(1)] Domicile of natural persons
To determine whether a party is domiciled in the Member State whose courts are seised, the court applies its own internal law.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.62(2)] Domicile of natural persons
If a party is not domiciled in the seised court's Member State, the court applies the law of another Member State to determine whether the party is domiciled there.

CASE FACTS:
Portuguese Party A and Irish Party B agreed in a written services contract that the Dublin courts 'have jurisdiction', without stating that jurisdiction is exclusive. A sues B in Dublin for service fees.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25] Choice-of-court agreements
Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(b)] Sale and service performance place
For a sale of goods, Article 7(1)(b) uses the place where the goods were or should have been delivered; for services, it uses the place where the services were or should have been provided.

CASE FACTS:
Portuguese Party A and Irish Party B agreed in a written services contract that the Dublin courts 'have jurisdiction', without stating that jurisdiction is exclusive. A sues B in Dublin for service fees.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25] Choice-of-court agreements
Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(b)] Sale and service performance place
For a sale of goods, Article 7(1)(b) uses the place where the goods were or should have been delivered; for services, it uses the place where the services were or should have been provided.

repair.prompt:
The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
An Italian court is first seised of A's tort action against B, which remains at first instance. A French court is later seised of A's contractual-liability action against C arising from the same investment project. C is domiciled in France, and the French court has an independent basis of international jurisdiction over the second action. The core facts substantially overlap and separate proceedings risk irreconcilable judgments. The Italian court has jurisdiction over both actions, and Italian law permits consolidation. C asks the French court to stay or decline jurisdiction under Article 30.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30] Related actions
Article 30 governs related actions pending in courts of different Member States and distinguishes discretionary stay from conditional decline.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(3)] Related actions
Actions are related when they are so closely connected that hearing them together is expedient to avoid irreconcilable judgments from separate proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(3)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Once the court designated in the agreement establishes jurisdiction, every court of another Member State must decline jurisdiction in its favour.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.26(1)] Appearance without jurisdiction objection
Apart from jurisdiction derived from other provisions of the Regulation, a court of a Member State before which a defendant enters an appearance has jurisdiction, except where the appearance was entered to contest jurisdiction or another court has exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

CASE FACTS:
British Party A and German Party B agreed that the courts of the United Kingdom would have exclusive jurisdiction. B first brings a negative declaratory action in Germany, and A later sues in the United Kingdom.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24] Exclusive jurisdiction
Article 24 assigns exclusive jurisdiction, regardless of the parties' domicile, for the listed subject matters.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25] Choice-of-court agreements
Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(1)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is rights in rem in, or tenancies of, immovable property are generally within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State where the property is situated, subject to the stated short private-tenancy exception.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(3)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is the validity of entries in public registers are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the register is kept.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(4)] Choice-of-court agreements
A jurisdiction agreement has no legal force if it conflicts with the specified protective-jurisdiction provisions or purports to exclude a court having exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.27] Own-motion review of exclusive jurisdiction
When the courts of another Member State have exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24, the court seised must declare of its own motion that it has no jurisdiction.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

British Party A and German Party B agreed that the courts of the United Kingdom would have exclusive jurisdiction. B first brings a negative declaratory action in Germany, and A later sues in the United Kingdom.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24] Exclusive jurisdiction
Article 24 assigns exclusive jurisdiction, regardless of the parties' domicile, for the listed subject matters.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25] Choice-of-court agreements
Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(1)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is rights in rem in, or tenancies of, immovable property are generally within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State where the property is situated, subject to the stated short private-tenancy exception.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(3)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is the validity of entries in public registers are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the register is kept.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(4)] Choice-of-court agreements
A jurisdiction agreement has no legal force if it conflicts with the specified protective-jurisdiction provisions or purports to exclude a court having exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.27] Own-motion review of exclusive jurisdiction
When the courts of another Member State have exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24, the court seised must declare of its own motion that it has no jurisdiction.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
An Irish court hears an employment-contract action brought by employer A against French employee B. B appears and argues the merits, but the file contains no indication that the court informed B of the right to contest jurisdiction.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.22(1)] Employer actions against employees
An employer generally may bring proceedings against an employee only in the courts of the Member State in which the employee is domiciled.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.26(1)] Appearance without jurisdiction objection
Apart from jurisdiction derived from other provisions of the Regulation, a court of a Member State before which a defendant enters an appearance has jurisdiction, except where the appearance was entered to contest jurisdiction or another court has exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(4)] Choice-of-court agreements
A jurisdiction agreement has no legal force if it conflicts with the specified protective-jurisdiction provisions or purports to exclude a court having exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.26(2)] Jurisdiction by appearance
For specified weaker parties, jurisdiction based on appearance requires the court to ensure that the defendant was informed of the right to contest jurisdiction and of the consequences of appearing or not appearing.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.26(1)] Appearance without jurisdiction objection
Apart from jurisdiction derived from other provisions of the Regulation, a court of a Member State before which a defendant enters an appearance has jurisdiction, except where the appearance was entered to contest jurisdiction or another court has exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
A Polish court was first seised but later found that it lacked jurisdiction and dismissed the action. Proceedings concerning the same dispute had also been filed in the Netherlands shortly before that dismissal.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

CASE FACTS:
Spanish seller A and Italian buyer B conclude a sales contract by telephone. A alleges that they orally agreed on the Vienna courts; B denies this, and the written contract contains no such clause.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(b)] Sale and service performance place
For a sale of goods, Article 7(1)(b) uses the place where the goods were or should have been delivered; for services, it uses the place where the services were or should have been provided.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25] Choice-of-court agreements
Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

repair.prompt:
The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
An Italian court is first seised of A's tort action against B, which remains at first instance. A French court is later seised of A's contractual-liability action against C arising from the same investment project. C is domiciled in France, and the French court has an independent basis of international jurisdiction over the second action. The core facts substantially overlap and separate proceedings risk irreconcilable judgments. The Italian court has jurisdiction over both actions, and Italian law permits consolidation. C asks the French court to stay or decline jurisdiction under Article 30.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30] Related actions
Article 30 governs related actions pending in courts of different Member States and distinguishes discretionary stay from conditional decline.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(3)] Related actions
Actions are related when they are so closely connected that hearing them together is expedient to avoid irreconcilable judgments from separate proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(3)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Once the court designated in the agreement establishes jurisdiction, every court of another Member State must decline jurisdiction in its favour.

The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
French consumer A orders furniture online from Dutch trader B. By a separate confirmation, A accepts a preselected term granting the Amsterdam courts exclusive jurisdiction. A later sues B in Amsterdam for performance.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.17(1)(c)] Consumer contract scope
The protective consumer-contract rules apply where the trader pursues or directs commercial activities to the consumer's Member State in the circumstances specified by this provision.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.18(1)] Jurisdiction for consumer contracts
A consumer may sue the other contracting party either in the courts of that party's Member State of domicile or, regardless of that party's domicile, in the courts for the place where the consumer is domiciled.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.18(2)] Jurisdiction for consumer contracts
The other contracting party may sue a consumer only in the courts of the Member State in which the consumer is domiciled.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.19] Choice-of-court limits in consumer contracts
A choice-of-court agreement in a consumer contract may depart from the protective jurisdiction rules only under the conditions stated in this provision.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24] Exclusive jurisdiction
Article 24 assigns exclusive jurisdiction, regardless of the parties' domicile, for the listed subject matters.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25] Choice-of-court agreements
Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(4)] Choice-of-court agreements
A jurisdiction agreement has no legal force if it conflicts with the specified protective-jurisdiction provisions or purports to exclude a court having exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.4(1)] General jurisdiction by defendant domicile
A person domiciled in a Member State is generally sued in the courts of that Member State, irrespective of nationality.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(1)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is rights in rem in, or tenancies of, immovable property are generally within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State where the property is situated, subject to the stated short private-tenancy exception.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(3)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is the validity of entries in public registers are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the register is kept.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.26(2)] Jurisdiction by appearance
For specified weaker parties, jurisdiction based on appearance requires the court to ensure that the defendant was informed of the right to contest jurisdiction and of the consequences of appearing or not appearing.

The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
Multinational company B is registered in Germany, has its central administration in France, and has its principal place of business in Spain. Party A sues B in France on an ordinary debt.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.4(1)] General jurisdiction by defendant domicile
A person domiciled in a Member State is generally sued in the courts of that Member State, irrespective of nationality.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(2)] Validity of companies and corporate decisions
Proceedings principally concerned with the validity, nullity, or dissolution of a company or the validity of decisions of its organs are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the company has its seat.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.32(1)] When a court is deemed seised
The time when a court is deemed seised depends on lodging the initiating document with the court or the authority responsible for service, provided the claimant takes the required subsequent steps.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.63(1)(b)] Domicile of companies and legal persons
For purposes of the Regulation, a company or other legal person is domiciled at its central administration.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.63(1)(c)] Domicile of companies and legal persons
For purposes of the Regulation, a company or other legal person is domiciled at its principal place of business.

The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
An Austrian court is first seised of A's contractual action against B but later finds that it lacks jurisdiction and dismisses the action. Proceedings concerning the same contract had been filed in Belgium shortly before the dismissal.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

CASE FACTS:
Party A owns an EU trade mark registered by the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO). Party B does not raise invalidity as a counterclaim in infringement proceedings, but instead brings a standalone action before a German court seeking a declaration that the EU trade mark is invalid.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[EU_TRADE_MARK_REGULATION:Art.63(1)] Application for revocation or invalidity
An application for revocation or for a declaration of invalidity of an EU trade mark may be submitted to the European Union Intellectual Property Office by the persons and groups specified in this paragraph.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(4)] Validity of registered intellectual property
Proceedings concerned with the registration or validity of patents, trade marks, designs, or other similar rights required to be deposited or registered fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the deposit or registration has been applied for, has taken place, or is deemed to have taken place, irrespective of whether the issue is raised by way of an action or as a defence.

[EU_TRADE_MARK_REGULATION:Art.124(d)] EU trade mark court jurisdiction
EU trade mark courts have exclusive jurisdiction over counterclaims for revocation or for a declaration of invalidity of an EU trade mark under Article 128.

[EU_TRADE_MARK_REGULATION:Art.128(1)] Counterclaims for revocation or invalidity
A counterclaim for revocation or for a declaration of invalidity may rely only on grounds for revocation or invalidity stated in the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.32(1)] When a court is deemed seised
The time when a court is deemed seised depends on lodging the initiating document with the court or the authority responsible for service, provided the claimant takes the required subsequent steps.

[EU_TRADE_MARK_REGULATION:Art.135] Coordination with other actions
A national court dealing with an EU-trade-mark action other than an action listed in Article 124 must treat the EU trade mark as valid.

CASE FACTS:
An Austrian court is first seised of A's contractual action against B but later finds that it lacks jurisdiction and dismisses the action. Proceedings concerning the same contract had been filed in Belgium shortly before the dismissal.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(1)] Mandatory stay for same cause and parties
Where proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties are brought in different Member States, a court other than the court first seised must stay its proceedings of its own motion.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties
On request, a court seised of the dispute must promptly inform another seised court of the date on which it was seised under Article 32.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions
When related actions are pending in courts of different Member States, a court other than the court first seised may stay its proceedings.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Article 31 addresses competing exclusive-jurisdiction claims and priority for a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement; it is distinct from Articles 29 and 30.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.31(2)] Exclusive-jurisdiction and chosen-court priority
Without prejudice to Article 26, where a court designated by an exclusive Article 25 agreement is seised, any court of another Member State must stay proceedings until the designated court declares that it has no jurisdiction under the agreement.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29] Same cause and same parties
Where courts of different Member States are seised of proceedings involving the same cause of action and the same parties, a court other than the court first seised must stay proceedings of its own motion and later defer if the first court's jurisdiction is established.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(2)] Same cause and same parties

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.29(3)] Same cause and same parties
Once the jurisdiction of the court first seised is established, every other court must decline jurisdiction in favour of that court.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(1)] Related actions

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

In matters relating to tort or delict, proceedings may be brought in the courts for the place where the harmful event occurred or may occur.

CASE FACTS:
A German court hears a dispute concerning rights in rem in French immovable property. Party B appears and argues the merits without contesting jurisdiction.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.26(1)] Appearance without jurisdiction objection
Apart from jurisdiction derived from other provisions of the Regulation, a court of a Member State before which a defendant enters an appearance has jurisdiction, except where the appearance was entered to contest jurisdiction or another court has exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24] Exclusive jurisdiction
Article 24 assigns exclusive jurisdiction, regardless of the parties' domicile, for the listed subject matters.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(1)] Exclusive jurisdiction
Proceedings whose object is rights in rem in, or tenancies of, immovable property are generally within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State where the property is situated, subject to the stated short private-tenancy exception.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.27] Own-motion review of exclusive jurisdiction
When the courts of another Member State have exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24, the court seised must declare of its own motion that it has no jurisdiction.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

The prior decision failed the frozen deterministic audit.

CASE FACTS:
An Italian court hears an action seeking a declaration that a trade mark registered in Germany is invalid. The defendant appears and argues the merits without contesting jurisdiction.

RETRIEVED LEGAL EVIDENCE:
[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.26(1)] Appearance without jurisdiction objection
Apart from jurisdiction derived from other provisions of the Regulation, a court of a Member State before which a defendant enters an appearance has jurisdiction, except where the appearance was entered to contest jurisdiction or another court has exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.24(4)] Validity of registered intellectual property
Proceedings concerned with the registration or validity of patents, trade marks, designs, or other similar rights required to be deposited or registered fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Member State in which the deposit or registration has been applied for, has taken place, or is deemed to have taken place, irrespective of whether the issue is raised by way of an action or as a defence.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.32(1)] When a court is deemed seised
The time when a court is deemed seised depends on lodging the initiating document with the court or the authority responsible for service, provided the claimant takes the required subsequent steps.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.4(1)] General jurisdiction by defendant domicile
A person domiciled in a Member State is generally sued in the courts of that Member State, irrespective of nationality.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25] Choice-of-court agreements
Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.28(1)] Default of appearance
If a defendant domiciled in one Member State is sued in another Member State and does not appear, the court must declare of its own motion that it lacks jurisdiction unless jurisdiction follows from the Regulation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.30(2)] Related actions
While the first-seised action is pending at first instance, another court may, on a party's application, decline jurisdiction if the first court has jurisdiction over the actions and its law permits consolidation.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(a)] Special jurisdiction
In matters relating to a contract, a defendant domiciled in a Member State may be sued in another Member State at the place of performance of the obligation in question.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.7(1)(b)] Sale and service performance place
For a sale of goods, Article 7(1)(b) uses the place where the goods were or should have been delivered; for services, it uses the place where the services were or should have been provided.

Article 25 governs agreements conferring jurisdiction on a court or the courts of a Member State.

[BRUSSELS_I_BIS:Art.25(1)] Choice-of-court agreements
A choice-of-court agreement satisfying the stated formal and substantive conditions confers jurisdiction on the designated Member State court and is exclusive unless the parties agree otherwise.

Electronic communication that provides a durable record of a jurisdiction agreement is equivalent to writing.

Where the specified EU service instrument does not apply, the identified Hague Service Convention rule applies if the initiating document had to be transmitted abroad.
